_about: The vocabulary a World Bible place list may use. Generated by tools/export_place_vocab.py from rules/places.py and rules/floorplan.py — do not edit by hand. The contract it belongs to is docs/places-and-races-for-world-bible.md.

id_grammar.why: terrain_of() parses this and never looks anything up, so an id without its ~terrain segment describes a place standing on nothing and the consumer builds open ground.

vertical.ledge: a raised band along one side with a rail at its lip to shoot over — a gallery, a landing over a hall, a wall-walk, a quay
vertical.slope: ground that climbs across the place — hills, a mountain path, an approach, dunes
vertical.scatter: isolated raised things and no rail — crates, rubble, a cart, roots
vertical.none: flat, and meant to be — a sump, an alley between two walls, farmland, open steppe

vertical_balance.why: the standing instruction is that a generated place is more likely to have verticality than not, without being silly about it. This is what the consumer's own tables came out at.

words.some: a few things to put between you and an arrow
words.cluttered: you cannot cross it in a straight line
words.dense: stalls, stacks or trunks, and sight lines of a few squares

words.broken: rubble, roots, spoil — slower in patches
words.bad: standing water, deep sand, a floor that is mostly not floor

ceilings_ft.why: a house is enough air to stand in and none to fly in. null means open sky, and the consumer treats the place as outdoors.

size_ft.why: the range the consumer's own tables cover. Nothing clamps an authored value yet, because nothing reads one.
